To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a compression ratio of 7.8:1 (compared to 8:1 for lossless compression) is sufficient for the majority of tasks in microarray data analysis, and that the scheme allows for a trade-off between compression and image quality, with the latter being a function of the task.

a partially progressive compression algorithm for cDNA microarray (and other) images is developed, that the compression rate of 4.5 bpp is sufficient for the majority of tasks, such as segmentation and extraction of expression levels, that the lossless bitrate is comparable to the state of the art, and that the algorithm has been tested on images of varying qualities from different labs.

a compression rate of 4.2 bpp (compared to 32 bpp for the uncompressed images) is sufficient for the majority of the image processing tasks, and that the lossless rate is about 17 bpp, competitive with the state-of-the art lossless schemes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the compression and processing of cDNA microarrays images.
the compression of images that are produced by the cDNA microarray technology.

compression, progressive compression, and lossy compression of microarray images, and we have developed a compression scheme which can be used to compress images in a progressive manner, with a lossy compression rate of 4.2 bits/pixel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our scheme is an excellent candidate for efficient transmission of microarray images.
the proposed scheme is a good compromise between compression ratio, speed of decoding, and image quality.
our compression method is a very useful tool for microarray image compression and transmission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed and implemented a compression algorithm that can be used for transmission of microarray images with a high level of compression.

our method provides an excellent compromise between lossless and lossy compression, with the added advantage of being able to trade off compression efficiency and image quality on a local basis, and to provide fast decodable subsets.
the proposed compression scheme can provide a good balance among compression efficiency, flexibility, and speed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compression of cDNA microarrays is not only possible, but can be performed at a rate low enough that transmission of the data over the internet is feasible.
the loss of information in the compression process is often not as important as the ability to process subsets of images in real-time.
the lossy rate-distortion performance is comparable to state-of-the-art methods, yet our scheme allows for progressive decoding, and locally varying loss.
